processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Three austenitic LDS grades (including the Ni-free 28Mn0Ni / Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C) were prepared by vacuum induction melting; the ingot weighed 30 kg. This is the as-cast part of the 'as-cast plus homogenised' condition.

The defect-free portions of the 30 kg as-cast ingots were homogenised at 1423 K for two hours. This is the homogenisation stage of the as-cast plus homogenised (as-homogenised) condition of 28Mn0Ni; the sample is the precursor/starting condition prior to hot rolling at 1323 K.

structures.overall_structure: As-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni alloy: primarily made of a single phase - equiaxed austenite (γ) grains containing straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles; essentially a single-phase austenitic structure (no B2, this being the B2-free grade).

characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructural observation of the as-cast plus homogenised 28Mn0Ni alloy sample (shown in Fig. 1a).
characterization_methods.key_findings: Equiaxed austenite grains with straight annealing twins and sparse dark particles; essentially single phase (no B2, consistent with the B2-free grade).

unmapped_findings: Chemical composition of the homogenised 28Mn0Ni (Fe-28Mn-9Al-0.9C) ingot in wt% (Table 1, analysed by wet chemical method/standard emission spectroscopy): Mn 28.3, Al 9.0, C 0.9, Ni not added (-), Fe balance. This is the analysed composition of the homogenised ingot from which this sample is taken.

28Mn0Ni is the Ni-free, B2-free grade of the study; its as-cast plus homogenised microstructure is primarily a single phase (austenite), in contrast to the Ni-containing 28Mn5Ni and 15Mn5Ni grades which are two-phase in the same condition.

This as-homogenised 28Mn0Ni ingot is the precursor/starting condition prior to hot rolling (hot rolling was subsequently carried out at 1323 K with ~85% total thickness reduction and ~15% reduction per pass); the mechanical properties, phase fractions and TEM/EBSD data reported elsewhere in the paper are for the hot-rolled condition and therefore do not apply to this as-homogenised sample.
